headline: Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Uchida said AI has so far pushed up demand and prices and loosened financial conditions, and warned of a correction if company profits do not follow.
score_reason: Fresh central bank speech, read via a secondhand summary because Bloomberg is blocked; score unchanged.
importance_line: It affects Japanese households and borrowers because rate decisions follow such views, and global bond investors, but Uchida gave no signal on rate timing.
summary: investingLive reports that Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Uchida said on Sunday that AI has so far acted as a large demand boost that raises prices and eases financial conditions, and that a correction is possible if corporate profits fail to keep pace with the AI investment boom. He said AI also affects benchmarks such as the neutral interest rate, the rate that neither speeds up nor slows the economy, but did not comment directly on the near-term path of rates.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (403). Text read at investingLive, which gives no source for the speech; the pool credit was Bloomberg and its headline matches the same remarks. Analyst commentary in that piece (hawkish lean, yen) was left out as opinion.
